meta.title: Operation of Refractometer in Central Instrumentation Laboratory

sections.purpose: To measure the refractive index and Brix (sugar content) of pharmaceutical solutions, syrups, oils, and liquid preparations for identity, purity assessment, and concentration determination as per pharmacopeial requirements.
sections.scope: Applicable to Central Instrumentation Laboratory for refractive index determination of liquid pharmaceuticals, essential oils, vegetable oils, and sugar-based preparations as per IP/BP identity tests.
procedure: Switch on the digital refractometer (or allow the Abbe refractometer to equilibrate to room temperature).
Set the temperature to 20°C using the thermostatic water circulation unit (for Abbe refractometer); digital refractometers with built-in ATC are ready after self-calibration.
Calibrate the refractometer with distilled water: nD₂₀ of water = 1.3330. Adjust if the reading does not match.
Clean the prism surface with a single pass of lens paper dampened with distilled water; blot dry — never rub.
Apply 2–3 drops of the sample to the illuminated prism using a clean, dry dropper or glass rod.
Close the sample lid (Abbe) to spread the sample in a thin film; for digital — simply apply and wait.
Adjust the illumination (Abbe: rotate the lamp arm) to obtain a clear light-dark boundary in the eyepiece field.
Bring the crosshair onto the light-dark boundary using the micrometer screw.
Read the refractive index on the scale (to 4 decimal places) or the digital display.
Repeat the measurement two more times; report the mean.
Clean the prism after each sample: wipe with a lens paper dampened with ethanol; allow to dry.
Compare the measured refractive index against the pharmacopeial value for the sample.
Record: sample name, refractive index (mean), temperature, and compliance status in the register.
precautions: Clean the prism with lens paper only — rough tissues and cotton scratch the prism surface permanently.
Never apply pressure to the prism cover when closing — cracking the prism is a costly irreversible damage.
Rinse with distilled water and dry the prism between different samples — residue from the previous sample contaminates the next reading.
Apply temperature correction if measuring at a temperature other than 20°C — refractive index changes approximately 0.00045 per °C for most liquids.
Use small sample volumes — 2–3 drops is sufficient; excess sample runs off the prism and wastes material.
Calibrate at the beginning of each day using distilled water.
Store the refractometer with the prism clean and dry; cover the prism with the protective cover.
